name: Oregon
nameStory: Nobody knows. Oregon is the great unsolved mystery of American place names. The leading theories are a mapmaker's misprint of an old name for the Wisconsin River, a Spanish word for 'big-eared,' and a French word for storm. Historians have argued about it for 200 years without settling it.
capitalStory: Salem is an English spelling of 'shalom' - peace. Missionaries named it, and it beat out bigger rivals for the capital largely because it was already the mission headquarters when the question came up.

funFacts: Crater Lake is 1,943 feet deep and sits in the collapsed crater of Mount Mazama, which blew itself apart about 7,700 years ago.
Every inch of Oregon's coastline is public property by law, thanks to a 1967 act - no private beaches anywhere in the state.
The Cascades split Oregon into two climates: rainforest on the west side, high desert on the east.
The Columbia River Gorge is the only near-sea-level route through the entire Cascade Range, which is why every road, rail line, and barge uses it.
